Like {{ill|Kawarabuchi Shrine|ja|河原淵神社}}, which is also an auxiliary shrine of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|外宮|lt=Outer Shrine}}, and {{ill|Kawara Shrine (Geku)|ja|毛理神社|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 河原神社 (伊勢市)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q17228197}}, which is enshrined together with Kawara Shrine, the three are collectively known as the "Mitsu-sha" (Three Shrines). According to ancient texts, Kawara Shrine is located north of Kawarabuchi Shrine<ref name="uy1">Ujiyamada City Office (1929): vol. 2, p. 911</ref>. Some theories suggest that Kawara Shrine was originally situated at the site of Hinokijiri Shrine along the Hinokijiri River in {{ill|Funae|ja|船江 (伊勢市)|qid=Q17213313}}, but during the Edo period, when Kawarabuchi Shrine was restored, Hinokijiri Shrine was identified with Kawarabuchi Shrine's site. As a result, Kawara Shrine was reconstructed further north in Misato-cho Shinkai, Ise<ref name="uy1"/>.

== Kawara Shrine ==

Kawara Shrine Ranks 11th among the 16 auxiliary shrines of the Outer Shrine. Its {{ill|Saijin|ja|Kami|lt=Deity}} is the {{ill|River deity|ja|川神|qid=DELETED_QID}}<ref name="ic"/>. The deity serves as the {{ill|Guardian deities|ja|守護神|qid=Q131278957|lt=Guardian deity}} of the lower reaches of the {{ill|Miya River (Mie)|en|Miya River (Mie)|qid=Q6884164|lt=Miyagawa River}} and also protects the rice fields<ref name="ic"/><ref name="gk">Gakken Publishing (2013): p. 63</ref>.

Although the enshrined deity of the former site of Hinokijiri Shrine in Funae, Ise, was unknown, it was decided to enshrine the River deity from Kawara Shrine due to its historical connection<ref name="uy4">Ujiyamada City Office (1929): vol. 2, p. 914</ref>. Hinokijiri Shrine was relocated to the same site as Kawarabuchi Shrine<ref name="uy4"/>.

== Mori Shrine ==

Mori Shrine Ranks 6th among the 8 subsidiary shrines of the Outer Shrine. Its enshrined deity is the {{ill|Tree deity|ja|木神|qid=Q140446141}}<ref name="ic"/>. This deity is regarded as the spirit of the {{ill|Shinboku|en|Shinboku|qid=Q48743901|lt=sacred tree}} in the forest where the shrine is located<ref name="ic"/><ref name="gk"/>.

It is believed that the site of Mori Shrine corresponds to the former location of Shigai Shrine in Misato-cho Shinkai<ref name="uy2">Ujiyamada City Office (1929): vol. 2, p. 912</ref>. Shigai Shrine was later relocated to the same site as Kawarabuchi Shrine<ref name="uy4"/>.

== History ==

According to the definition of Ise Jingū's subsidiary shrines, Mori Shrine was established before the compilation of the {{ill|Enryaku Gishikichō|ja|延暦儀式帳|lt=Enryaku Gishiki-chō}}, i.e., before {{ill|Enryaku|en|Enryaku|qid=Q1373176|lt=Enryaku}} 23 (804). Based on the definition of auxiliary shrines, Kawara Shrine was established before the compilation of the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳}}, i.e., before {{ill|Enchō|ja|延長|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q97379316}} 5 (927)<ref>Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 22</ref>. 

During the {{ill|Middle Ages|en|Middle Ages|qid=Q12554|lt=medieval period}}, rituals were discontinued, and by the {{ill|Early modern period|an|Edat Moderna|ar|الحقبة الحديثة المبكرة|ast|Edá Moderna|az|Erkən modern dövr|bar|Friae Neizeid|be|Ранні Новы час|bn|প্রারম্ভিক আধুনিক যুগ|br|Amzerioù modern|ca|Edat moderna|cs|Raný novověk|cy|Cyfnod Modern Cynnar|da|Tidlig moderne tid|de|Frühe Neuzeit|el|Πρώιμη νεότερη περίοδος|eo|Frua moderna epoko|es|Edad Moderna|et|Varauusaeg|eu|Aro Modernoa|fa|دوران نوین آغازین|fi|Varhaismoderni|fr|Époque moderne|gl|Idade Moderna|gn|Ára Ko'ãgagua|he|העת החדשה המוקדמת|hi|प्रारंभिक आधुनिक काल|hu|Korai újkor|ia|Etate Moderne|id|Periode modern awal|io|Modern-epoko|it|Età moderna|ja|近世|kbp|Alɩwaatʊ kɩfatʊ (Période moderne)|ko|근세|ku|Destpêka Dema Nûjen|kw|Oos Arnowydh A-Varr|lb|Neizäit|lfn|Eda moderna|li|Vreugmodernen Tied|lij|Etæ Modèrna|lld|Storia moderna|lmo|Età Modèrna|lo|ຍຸກ​ສະ​ໄຫມ​ຕົ້ນ​|lt|Naujieji amžiai|lv|Agrīnie jaunie laiki|mg|Andro Vaovao|mk|Ран нов век|new|प्रारम्भिक आधुनिक काल|nl|Vroegmoderne tijd|nn|Tidleg nytid|no|Tidlig moderne tid|oc|Edat Modèrna|pap|Edad Moderno|pcd|Histoère modérne|pl|Nowożytność|ps|لومړۍ معاصره دوره|pt|Idade Moderna|rm|Temp modern tempriv|ro|Epoca modernă timpurie|ru|Раннее Новое время|sc|Edade moderna|sh|Rani novi vijek|simple|Early modern period|sq|Periudha e hershme moderne|sr|Rani novi vek|stq|Eermodärne Tied|sv|Tidigmoderna tiden|th|สมัยใหม่ตอนต้น|tl|Makabagong kasaysayan|tr|Yeni Çağ|tt|Иртә яңа заман|uk|Ранній новий період|vi|Thời kỳ cận đại|vls|Nieuwn tyd|wuu|近世|yi|נייע צייט|zh|近世|zh_yue|近代史|qid=Q5308718|lt=early modern period}}, the shrine sites had become unknown. In {{ill|Kanbun (era)|en|Kanbun (era)|qid=Q1146228|lt=Kanbun}} 3 (1663), {{ill|Kiyonaga Kawabe|ja|河辺精長|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q92924151}} (also known as Ōnakatomi Masanaga) restored the shrines at their current locations<ref>Furan Ken, "[https://web.archive.org/web/20150610132106/http://www.geocities.jp/engisiki/ise/bun/is080144-01.html Kawara Shrine]" (Accessed September 29, 2013)</ref>.

== Flora ==

A large {{ill|Camphora officinarum|en|Camphora officinarum|qid=Q158722|lt=camphor tree}} stands behind the {{ill|Shinto architecture|ar|عمارة الشنتو|de|Japanische Schreinarchitektur|fr|Architecture shinto|he|אדריכלות השינטו|hu|Sintó építészet|id|Arsitektur jinja|it|Architettura shintoista|ja|神社建築|ru|Синтоистская архитектура|simple|Shinto architecture|sl|Šintoistična arhitektura|zh|神社建築|qid=Q3080012}}<ref name="ic"/><ref name="gk"/>. The {{ill|shin'iki|ja|神域|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11588853}} is well-maintained with neatly trimmed hedges<ref name="ic"/>.

== Access and Surroundings ==

Next to Kawara Shrine and Mori Shrine is a {{ill|Factory|en|Factory|qid=Q83405|lt=factory}} operated by Matsuya Confectionery, known for producing black candy<ref>Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 49</ref>. A 10-minute walk north along Ise City Road will lead to the site of the former {{ill|Yamada bugyō|ja|山田奉行所|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 山田奉行|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q4275043}}<ref name="gk"/>.

* About a 6-minute walk (approx. 500 m) from the "Shinkai" {{ill|Bus stop|en|Bus stop|qid=Q953806|lt=bus stop}} serviced by {{ill|Mie Kotsu|en|Mie Kotsu|qid=Q6843516|lt=Mie Kotsu}} buses.
* Approximately a 2-minute drive (approx. 800 m) north from the "Ogicho 1" {{ill|Intersection (road)|en|Intersection (road)|qid=Q285783|lt=intersection}} on {{ill|Japan National Route 23|en|Japan National Route 23|qid=Q5357579|lt=National Route 23}} ({{ill|Q11407535|ja|南勢バイパス|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11407535}}). No parking is available nearby.
